extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and supervisory personnel; patent practitioners involved in inter partes reexamination
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and criteria for determining whether a request for inter partes reexamination raises a "substantial new question of patentability" (SNQ), what prior art and claims are considered, and the required content/procedures for decisions granting or denying reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantial New Question of Patentability (SNQ) — basic test
rubrics_metrics.description: The presence or absence of 'a substantial new question of patentability' determines whether reexamination is ordered; the term is not defined in the statute and is developed case-by-case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the prior art patents and printed publications raise a substantial question of patentability of at least one claim, an SNQ is present unless the same question has already been decided by (A) a final holding of invalidity after all appeals, or (B) by the Office in a previous examination or pending/concluded reexamination. The Director's determination under 35 U.S.C. 312(c) is final.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable-examiner importance test
rubrics_metrics.description: A prior art patent or printed publication raises an SNQ where there is a substantial likelihood that a reasonable examiner would consider the prior art important in deciding whether the claim is patentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the prior art would be considered important, the examiner should find an SNQ unless the same question has already been decided. 'Important' is judged from the perspective of a reasonable examiner deciding claim patentability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Previous-examination / final-court-decision bar
rubrics_metrics.description: An SNQ is not present if the same question of patentability has been decided by a final holding of invalidity (after appeals) or has been decided by the Office in a previous examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 'previous examination' includes the original examination of the application, reissue examination that resulted in reissue, or examination in an earlier pending/concluded reexamination. Examiners should check file history for art previously cited/considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prima facie case not required for SNQ
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not necessary that a prima facie case of unpatentability exist for an SNQ to be present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An SNQ could be present even if the examiner would not necessarily reject the claim as anticipated or obvious over the prior art; distinguish SNQ from a prima facie rejection (see In re Etter).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of KSR on SNQ standard
rubrics_metrics.description: The KSR clarification of obviousness under 35 U.S.C. 103 does not alter the legal standard for determining whether an SNQ exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 2616 for discussion. SNQ standard for granting reexamination remains unchanged by KSR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second or subsequent request requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A second or subsequent request made while an earlier reexamination is pending may provide information raising an SNQ for new/amended claims, but to be granted it must independently provide an SNQ different from that raised in the pending reexamination for the claims in effect at the time of determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision is based on the claims in effect at the time (37 CFR 1.923). If no 'different' SNQ is provided for the existing claims, the subsequent request must be denied. Once a different SNQ is established for current claims, information directed to proposed new/amended claims in the pending reexam may also be considered to permit examination of the entire patent package.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner duty to check file history and 'old art'
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner should check the patent's file history to see whether prior art advanced by the requester was previously cited/considered ('old art').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the art was previously considered in an earlier examination, it may be 'old art.' For determinations on or after Nov. 2, 2002, reliance on old art does not necessarily preclude an SNQ — determinations are fact-specific. See In re Hiniker and Public Law 107-273.

rubrics_metrics.name: Old art can be sole basis for SNQ (Post-2002)
rubrics_metrics.description: Per Public Law 107-273 (effective Nov. 2, 2002), the existence of an SNQ is not precluded solely because the art was previously cited/considered by the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether an SNQ exists based solely on old art requires a fact-specific inquiry: e.g., old art presented/viewed in a new light, or in a different way, in view of a material new argument or interpretation. Use form paragraph 22.01.01 where SNQ is based solely on old art. Examiner notes specify how to fill form brackets and that paragraph used only the first time the 'already cited/considered' art is applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior favorable Office decisions on same art
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Office previously considered the same question of patentability based on the same prior art and made a favorable decision to the patent owner, that prior art does not raise an SNQ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference: In re Recreative Technologies. Where previously considered art is cumulative to art in earlier examination, it will not support an SNQ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior adverse Office decisions on same art
rubrics_metrics.description: A prior decision adverse to patentability of a claim by the Office based on prior art patents/printed publications would usually mean an SNQ is present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a reissue application abandoned after rejection without disclaiming the patent claim could support an SNQ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior adverse final decisions based on non-patent grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior adverse final decisions by the Director or the Board on a reissue application that were based on grounds other than patents or printed publications will not be considered in determining whether an SNQ exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such prior adverse decisions are considered by the examiner only to the extent they are based on patents/printed publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of decisions in other cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions involving substantially identical patents or publications in other cases may be considered in determining whether an SNQ is raised, with the weight given depending on the circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner should evaluate the relevance and weight of such external decisions on a case-by-case basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of federal court decisions on SNQ
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal court decisions affect SNQ as follows: (A) a final court decision of validity does not necessarily preclude an SNQ; (B) a non-final holding of invalidity/unenforceability is not controlling; (C) a final holding of invalidity or unenforceability after all appeals is controlling and precludes an SNQ for the claims finally held invalid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office may accord deference to factual findings by courts but determines SNQ independently. See Ethicon v. Quigg and related discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims considered — claims in effect at determination
rubrics_metrics.description: The claims of the patent in effect at the time of determination (37 CFR 1.923) are the basis for deciding whether an SNQ is present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reexamination determination generally limited to review of the claims for which reexamination was requested. 35 U.S.C. 311(b)(2) requires the requester to set forth pertinency and manner of applying cited prior art to every claim for which reexamination is requested; failure to apply art to certain claims generally means requester is not statutorily entitled to reexamination of those claims. The Office may, at its discretion, reexamine claims not requested or initiate reexam on its own.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copending amendments/new claims — not considered in deciding request
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments and/or new claims present in any copending reexamination or reissue proceeding will not be considered nor commented upon when deciding a request for reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, where reexamination is ordered, the first Office action (which ordinarily accompanies the order) and any subsequent reexamination prosecution should be on the basis of the claims as amended by any copending reexamination or reissue proceeding. See MPEP § 2640 subsection II.(A).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior art sources examiner may consider
rubrics_metrics.description: The determination whether an SNQ is present can be based upon any prior art patents or printed publications; the examiner is not limited to the art relied upon in the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner may base the SNQ on references in the request, a combination of requested art and other art, or entirely on different patents/printed publications. Examiner may consider patents/publications of record in the patent file (e.g., 37 CFR 1.501/1.98 submissions). If additional prior art can be readily obtained to supply deficiencies, examiner may perform a limited search focused on areas most likely to contain needed art, only where there is reasonable likelihood such art exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required content of decision granting reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Director finds an SNQ affecting a claim, the determination shall include an order for inter partes reexamination and the examiner's decision granting the request must (A) identify all claims and issues, (B) identify the patents and/or printed publications relied upon, and (C) provide a brief statement of the rationale supporting each new question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner must identify at least one SNQ and explain how the cited art raises that question. References relied on should be cited on proper PTO forms and copies supplied only where not previously provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision elements to 'point out' for each SNQ (A–F)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each SNQ identified, the decision should point out specific elements (A–F).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A) The prior art patents/printed publications which add some new teaching as to at least one claim; B) What that new teaching is; C) The claims that the new teaching is directed to; D) That the new teaching was not previously considered nor addressed in prior examination or a final court holding; E) That the new teaching is such that a reasonable examiner would consider it important in deciding to allow the claim; and F) Where raised or where it is unclear that a reference predates the patent claims, explain why the reference is deemed available against the claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper grounds excluded from reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Grounds not based on patents or printed publications (e.g., public use, on sale under 35 U.S.C. 102(b), abandonment under 35 U.S.C. 102(c)) are improper for reexamination and are not considered or commented upon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such matters should be noted as improper; they cannot be used to grant reexamination. See 37 CFR 1.906(c). They may be argued and appealed during the examination phase but are not grounds for the initial determination to order reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision granting request does not decide patentability
rubrics_metrics.description: In the decision on the request, the examiner will not decide, nor state, whether the claims are rejected over the patents and printed publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner only decides whether an SNQ exists to grant the request; the merits of patentability are addressed in the reexamination prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form/notice and timing requirements when granting
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph 26.01 should be used at the beginning of each decision letter granting reexamination; form paragraph 26.73 at the end when not mailed with first Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision granting the request is made using form PTOL-2063 as a cover sheet. Extensions of time under 37 CFR 1.136(a) are not permitted in inter partes reexamination (they apply only to 'an applicant'); 35 U.S.C. 314(c) requires inter partes reexam to be conducted with special dispatch. Patent owner extensions are provided under 37 CFR 1.956; third party requester comments have a statute-set 30-day period (35 U.S.C. 314(b)(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel review conference before issuing order
rubrics_metrics.description: Before issuing an order granting reexamination, the examiner informs the CRU SPE, who convenes a panel review conference to review the matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the conference confirms the examiner's preliminary decision, the proposed order is issued and signed by the examiner with two conferrees initialing. If not confirmed, the examiner reevaluates and issues appropriate communication. See MPEP § 2671.03 for panel makeup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition to vacate reexamination order — limited grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: A 37 CFR 1.181 petition may be filed to vacate an ultra vires reexamination order; substantive determinations to institute reexamination are not otherwise subject to petition or review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appropriate circumstances under 37 CFR 1.181(a)(3) include: (A) order not based on prior art patents/printed publications; (B) reexamination prohibited under 37 CFR 1.907; (C) all claims held invalid by final decision of a Federal Court after appeals; (D) reexamination ordered for wrong patent; (E) order based on duplicate copy of the request; (F) order based wholly on the same question of patentability previously considered in an earlier concluded Office examination. When a 1.181 petition is filed, the third party requester may file a single opposition within two weeks of service; courtesy phone call to CRU SPE recommended; opposition should be faxed when possible. The third party requester may file only a single submission in opposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of prior art citations submitted after the order
rubrics_metrics.description: Any prior art citations submitted under 37 CFR 1.501 after the date of the decision ordering inter partes reexamination should be retained separately by the Technology Center until the reexamination proceeding is concluded, at which time the citation is entered of record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 2206. Note 37 CFR 1.902 governs submissions of prior art that can be made by patent owners and third party requesters after reexamination has been ordered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision denying reexamination — required explanations per citation
rubrics_metrics.description: If no SNQ is found, the decision denying the reexamination request must explain, for each patent or publication cited, why it does not raise an SNQ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision should indicate whether the citation: (A) is cumulative to teachings of art cited in an earlier concluded examination; (B) is not available against the claims (e.g., due to date or not a publication); (C) would not be important to a reasonable examiner even if available and not cumulative; or (D) was cited in the patent record and is barred by MPEP § 2642 II.A guidelines. Examiner should also respond to substance of each argument raised by the third party requester that is based on patents/printed publications. Improper grounds based on non-patent evidence should be noted as not considered.
